answer: Each agent gets one active account only after posting a bond that is slashed if it double-signs or fails a randomly assigned task; rewards accrue gradually as peers verify useful work, and withdrawals wait through a challenge period. An attacker can still create many identities, but must lock capital in every one and keep each credible over time, while any detected equivocation burns its bond. The sonnet, ivory, and quill accounts face the same rule: identity is cheap; persistent, accountable participation is not.
